summary: Richard Wilhelm (1873–1930) was a sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen. He served as a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair for Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924.

Richard von Garbe (1857–1927) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann, Rudolf von Roth, and Bhagavata Acharya, earning degrees from Tübingen and Königsberg. He taught at Königsberg (1878–1895) and Tübingen (1895–1927).

Richard von Glahn (born 1953) is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988–1989) and became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987.

Rico Sennrich (born 1985) is a computational linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Zurich in 2013. He held posts at the University of Zurich around 2010 and served as a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh from 2015 to 2022.
Rigdzin Shikpo (1935–2023) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Helsinki. Her doctoral supervisors were Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and she also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rik Pinxten (born 1947) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He completed two doctorates at Ghent University in 1975 and served as a professor there from 1981 to 2012.

Rikizan Ishikawa (1943–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1971. He served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Komazawa University from around 1978 to 1997.

Ringu Tulku (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru.

Rinzin Thargyal was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.
Rita Gupta is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under David Friedman. She held an academic post at North-Eastern Hill University.

Rita Langer is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and earned a PhD from Hamburg in 2004, later joining the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross (1943–2015) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her dissertation at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of Philosophy and Religious Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire from around 1979 to 1998.

Rizong Sras Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure trained at Drepung Loseling Monastery under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as Abbot of Gyume Tantric College, Drepung Loseling, and Samstanling, and as 102nd Ganden Thripa.

Ričardas Mironas (1908–1979) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Vytautas Magnus University and the Sorbonne. He held posts as an assistant and associate professor at Vytautas Magnus University (1944–1946) and became a professor at Vilnius University in 1950.

Rob Linrothe (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and art history. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago and held academic posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn (1939–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Zimbabwe, Edinburgh, and London, and under the 14th Dalai Lama and 16th Karmapa. He held posts at the University of Zimbabwe (~1967–1976) and the University of Cape Town (~1977–1980).

Robert A. F. Thurman (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Geshe Wangyal and the 14th Dalai Lama. He held positions at Amherst College (1973–1988) and served as a director at Columbia University (1988–2019).

Robert A. Hall, Jr. (1911–1997) was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Sapienza, and Chicago, where he studied under Leonard Bloomfield and Carl Darling Buck. He taught at Puerto Rico, Princeton, and Brown, and was professor at Cornell (1946–1976).
